costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a G4FP typically takes 7-10 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for a G4FP is the condition of the direct‑injection fuel system and turbocharger. A used engine may have a failing high‑pressure fuel pump (HPFP) or clogged injectors, which add significant cost. A reconditioned unit should include new HPFP and injectors (or certification of correct operation), a rebuilt turbo with new bearings, and decarbonisation of the intake valves. Also check whether the 48V mild‑hybrid system (if fitted) is included; that adds complexity and cost. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for more detail.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the G4FP
variants.intro: The G4FP is a specific engine code within the Smartstream family. Unlike older Gamma engines, it has been produced with relatively few sub‑variants - the main differences are software tunes for different power outputs (150 hp, 180 hp, 204 hp) and the inclusion of a 48V mild‑hybrid starter‑generator on some applications (e.g. Tucson MHEV). Hardware is largely identical across the range. Key technical specifications: - Displacement: 1,598 cc - Bore × Stroke: 75.6 mm × 88.8 mm - Compression ratio: 10.0:1 - Cylinder block: Aluminium with cast‑iron liners - Cylinder head: Aluminium, 16‑valve DOHC, dual CVVT - Valvetrain: Hydraulic lash adjusters - Timing drive: Chain - Fuel system: Direct injection (GDI), max pressure 350 bar - Turbocharger: Single twin‑scroll with electric wastegate - Power output: 150 hp (low tune), 180 hp (mid), 204 hp (high/GT) - Torque: 265 Nm (low), 300 Nm (mid), 320 Nm (high) - Euro standard: Euro 6d‑TEMP / Euro 6d - Mild‑hybrid: Optional 48V system (MHEV) with integrated starter‑generator (ISG) Confusable codes: - G4FJ - The previous 1.6 T‑GDi (Gamma II) used in older Hyundai i30 and Kia Ceed; it has a different block casting, different injectors and a different turbo design. Not interchangeable. - G4FC - The naturally aspirated 1.6 MPI Gamma engine; completely different fuel system and no turbo. Do not confuse. - G4NA - The 2.0 Nu petrol; different displacement and architecture. Why fitting the wrong revision matters: Using a G4FJ in place of a G4FP will not physically fit (mounts and plumbing differ). Even among G4FP variants, the 48V mild‑hybrid versions have additional electrical connections and a different belt drive for the ISG - a non‑MHEV unit will not work in a MHEV vehicle. Always match the full engine code, including any suffix (e.g. G4FP…).

relatives.description: The Gamma II 1.6 T‑GDi that the Smartstream G4FP replaced in most applications. The G4FJ had a different block casting, older injector technology and a less efficient wastegate design. It suffered similar carbon build‑up and HPFP issues, but the G4FP’s revised cooling and improved injector angle reduce some of the earlier problems.

The Smartstream 1.6 T‑GDi continues in production with various hybridisations (48V and plug‑in). For some models, the G4FP is being replaced by larger 1.6‑litre turbo‑hybrid variants or Smartstream 2.0 T‑GDi in performance applications.

The 1.5‑litre Smartstream turbo petrol used in newer Hyundai/Kia models. It shares the same basic architecture but with a shorter stroke and lower displacement; often found in the latest Kona and Ceed.
A lower‑output 1.6 T‑GDi variant used in some markets (not common in UK); shares most hardware but with different engine control unit (ECU) calibration.

It also appears on the V5C registration document under "Engine number" (the first characters will be G4FP). buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement G4FP - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used G4FP can be a cost‑effective option for lower‑value vehicles (e.g. older Kona or i30) where a £2,200+ recon unit would be uneconomical. However, used engines are a significant gamble: the HPFP, turbo, and injectors may be nearing the end of their service life, and carbon build‑up is almost guaranteed. Only consider a used G4FP if it comes from a known low‑mileage (under 40,000 miles) post‑2021 vehicle, and if you factor in the cost of a new HPFP and an intake valve decarbonisation.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A properly reconditioned G4FP is the wisest choice for most owners. A quality recon should include: cylinder head disassembly with thorough decarbonisation (walnut‑blasting) of intake valves, new piston rings and bearings, new timing chain and tensioner, a new or reconditioned high‑pressure fuel pump, newly calibrated injectors, and a turbocharger rebuild with new bearings and seals. Most reconditioned units also come with a 12-24 month warranty, giving you protection that a used engine cannot offer.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild is justified when the vehicle is high‑value (e.g. a 1‑owner Tucson or Sportage with low body mileage) and you wish to preserve the original engine number. For the G4FP, an upgraded rebuild should include: upgraded HPFP (if available), a larger intercooler (for performance applications), and a walnut‑blast of the intake manifold. A rebuild is generally more expensive than a recon exchange, but it can be custom‑specified to your requirements.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All options can be supplied and fitted through our network of UK Hyundai/Kia specialists - we handle the logistics, warranty coordination and nationwide delivery so you get a turnkey solution.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The G4FP is found across a broad value spectrum - from £6,000-£12,000 older i30 and Kona examples, through £12,000-£22,000 Tucson and Sportage, up to £20,000-£35,000 newer Niro and Sportage MHEV models. **For vehicles valued under £7,000, a reconditioned G4FP at £2,200+ supply‑only represents 30-40% of the vehicle’s value - always compare against the vehicle's condition and your ownership horizon.** For higher‑value examples, the replacement cost is comfortably within the vehicle's worth and represents a sound investment in reliable motoring.

mainEntity.name: How much does a G4FP engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned G4FP supply-only unit typically costs £2,200-£3,500, with used units from £900-£1,800. Fitted prices add 7-10 hours of labour at independent specialist rates. Used G4FP engines: £900-£1,800 supply-only. Reconditioned G4FP: £2,200-£3,500 supply-only. Rebuilt G4FP: £3,200-£4,500 supply-only. Labour: 7-10 hours at approximately £65-£85 per hour.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the G4FP engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most frequently reported G4FP issues are: carbon build-up on intake valves due to direct injection, causing misfires and rough idle; high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) wear leading to hard starting and stalling; and turbocharger wastegate/actuator wear causing boost pressure faults. Carbon deposits on intake valves are almost universal after 30,000-60,000 miles. HPFP failure is common around 50,000-80,000 miles; pre-emptive replacement is recommended. Wastegate actuator wear can cause under-boost or over-boost faults.

mainEntity.name: Which Hyundai and Kia models use the G4FP engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The G4FP was introduced in 2018 and is fitted to many Hyundai and Kia compact and mid-size models, often badged as '1.6 T-GDi'. Hyundai models include i30 (PD and facelift), Tucson (TL and NX4), Kona (OS and SX2), Elantra (CN7), and Sonata (DN8). Kia models include Ceed (CD), ProCeed (CD), Sportage (QL and NQ5), Niro (DE and SG2), Soul (SK3), and K5 (DL3).

mainEntity.name: Should I buy a used or reconditioned G4FP?

acceptedAnswer.text: A used G4FP is a gamble unless it comes from a low-mileage (under 40,000 miles) post-2021 vehicle and you budget for a new HPFP and an intake decarbonisation. A reconditioned unit is the safer, more cost-effective option for most owners: it includes a rebuilt turbo, new HPFP, freshly calibrated injectors and a thorough decarbonisation of the intake valves. Recon units come with a 12-24 month warranty.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my car has the G4FP engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The G4FP engine code is stamped on a flat metal pad on the cylinder block, typically near the front above the starter motor or behind the alternator. It also appears on the V5C registration document under 'Engine number' (first characters G4FP). If unsure, enter your registration above and we'll confirm the exact fitment.

mainEntity.name: What is the lifespan of a G4FP engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance - regular oil changes (5W-30 every 6,000-8,000 miles), use of top-tier fuel, and occasional Italian tune-ups to reduce carbon build-up - the G4FP can reliably exceed 150,000 miles before major work is required. Pre-emptive replacement of the HPFP at 60,000 miles and decarbonisation at 50,000 miles will extend life significantly. Post-2021 units with revised HPFP and wastegate design are more durable.
